t: Alexander founded the city in 331 BCE and the Ptolemies, who ruled Egypt from it from 305 BCE, made it the largest city in the world within about a century, with a Library and Museion and the Pharos lighthouse.
Under Rome it remained a granary and a centre of Christian theology, but suffered riots, a massacre under Caracalla, a tsunami in 365 CE and the destruction of the Serapeum in 391.
After the Arab conquest of 641 the capital moved to Fustat; the city declined under the Ottomans and revived from about 1810 under Muhammad Ali, until the bombardment of 1882.
dyk: The Lighthouse of Alexandria, reputed to be 138 metres high, was begun by Ptolemy I and finished under Ptolemy II at a cost of 800 talents. Earthquakes destroyed it in the 14th century, and the Qaitbay citadel of 1477 stands on its site.
ev: Alexander the Great founds the city
Ptolemy declares himself Pharaoh and moves his capital from Memphis to Alexandria
Julius Caesar is besieged in the city, and the Library faces destruction
Theodosius I orders the destruction of pagan temples and the Serapeum is destroyed
The Arabs under Amr ibn al-As take the city after a siege of fourteen months
Crusaders led by Peter of Cyprus take and sack the city
French troops storm the city during Napoleon's expedition
British naval forces bombard and occupy the city

f.founded: April 331 BCE by Alexander the Great (the exact date is disputed), on the site of an Egyptian village called Rhakotis; the architect was Dinocrates of Rhodes
f.where: On the southern shore of the Mediterranean at the western edge of the Nile Delta, between the sea and Lake Mareotis, in northern Egypt
f.known: The Lighthouse of Alexandria (the Pharos); the Library and Museion; the Ptolemaic court; the Septuagint; the Patriarchate of Alexandria; the Serapeum; the medieval spice trade; the bombardment of 1882
f.today: Alexandria is the second largest city of Egypt after Cairo and its principal seaport.
